title: Administrative & Procurement Assistant
description:
An excellent opportunity for an Administrative & Procurement Assistant to join a well-established company based in Birtley, Gateshead

Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent

Location: Gateshead, DH3

Salary: 28,000 per annum, depending on experience

Reports to: Finance Manager

About the Role:

The administrative and procurement assistant role is to provide effective administrative and procurement support to the business, ensuring that purchasing activities, project-related orders, supplier requirements, documentation and general office administration are managed accurately, efficiently and in accordance with company procedures.

Main Duties:

Administrative responsibilities
- Answer incoming telephone calls professionally and direct enquiries to the appropriate person or department.
- Scan, organise and archive delivery notes in accordance with company procedures.
- Regularly monitor outstanding certificates and follow up with relevant parties to ensure required documentation is received and maintained.
- Complete meter reading submissions accurately and within required deadlines.
- Manage stationery requirements and place orders to ensure adequate office supplies are maintained.
- Provide general administrative support to the wider team and assist with other office requirements as necessary.

Procurement Responsibilities
- Raise and process purchase orders for ongoing projects, ensuring orders accurately reflect project requirements and are raised within required timescales.
- Liaise with project teams to obtain the necessary information and approvals required to support purchasing activities.
- Process proforma invoices and online orders in accordance with company purchasing procedures.
- Regularly review outstanding purchase orders and proactively follow up with suppliers regarding overdue orders, supporting the timely delivery of goods and services to projects.
- Respond to and resolve purchase order queries, liaising with suppliers and internal departments as required.
- Manage PPE ordering, ensuring requirements are identified and orders are placed in a timely manner.
- Maintain appropriate purchasing records and ensure relevant documentation is complete and accurately recorded.
- Develop and maintain effective working relationships with suppliers and internal stakeholders to support the smooth running of procurement activities.
- Provide general procurement support to project teams and the wider business as required.

Candidate Requirements:
- Strong administrative, organisational and procurement skills.
- Good attention to detail and accuracy.
- Confident communication skills, both verbal and written.
- Professional telephone manner.
- Previous experience in a procurement, purchasing, procurement administration or similar role.
- Ability to communicate effectively with suppliers, project teams and internal colleagues.
- Proactive approach to chasing outstanding orders, deliveries and documentation.
- Ability to prioritise and manage multiple project and administrative tasks.
- Good computer literacy and ability to learn relevant purchasing and business systems.
- Reliable, methodical and organised approach to work.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- Ability to follow company processes and procedures consistently.
- Ability to work to deadlines and respond effectively to changing project requirements.
- Eligible to work permanently in the UK.
- Full driving licence

If you feel that you have the relative skills/attributes to fulfil this role then please apply now!

The employer fully supports Equality in Employment. All employment is decided based on qualifications, merit and business need.

title: Client Retentions & Renewals Adviser
description:
Client Retention & Renewals Adviser

Gateshead 31,734 + Bonus Realistic OTE 37,734

Represent the Business. Own the Relationship. Protect the Contract.

Office Angels are recruiting for a Client Retention & Renewals Adviser to join a successful and established organisation based in Gateshead. This is a high-quality, client-facing commercial role for someone confident building relationships, managing renewals and discussing contracts, pricing and value with key stakeholders.

As a Client Retention & Renewals Executive, you'll become a key point of contact for an established portfolio of clients across the UK. You'll conduct client meetings via video and telephone, manage commercial renewal conversations and build relationships with key stakeholders. You'll understand client requirements, discuss contracts and pricing, address concerns and ensure clients continue to see value in their relationship with the business.

This is not a high-volume contact centre environment. You'll manage relationships, own renewal opportunities and represent the business directly to clients.

What You'll Get
- 31,734 basic + monthly performance-related bonus Realistic OTE 37,734
- Monday to Friday 8:30am to 4:30pm No weekends
- Hybrid working after qualifying service
- Company pension
- Health Shield, including private dental and medical benefits
- Employee discounts and wellbeing platform
- Full product and systems training
- Ongoing career development
- Central Gateshead location with excellent transport links

Holiday Set Up
- Up to 37 days' annual leave including Bank Holidays
- Annual leave is be taken during half term periods, with up to two days' annual leave permitted during each term
- During August, working hours are reduced to 9:30am to 3:00pm
- Five days' annual leave are allocated to the August wellbeing shutdown week, with additional shutdown over Christmas

A Commercial Role With Real Responsibility

You'll manage a portfolio of existing clients and renewal opportunities, taking ownership throughout the renewal journey. Clients may be responsible for significant purchasing decisions, so you'll need to be comfortable having commercial conversations around contracts, pricing, value and requirements. You'll identify potential renewal risks, explore concerns directly and represent the business with professionalism and credibility.

What You'll Be Doing
- Managing client relationships throughout the renewal lifecycle
- Conducting professional client meetings via video, telephone and email
- Building trusted relationships with key contacts and stakeholders
- Understanding client requirements, objectives and concerns
- Managing renewals through to completion
- Discussing contracts, pricing, terms and renewal options
- Preparing quotations and commercial proposals
- Handling objections and identifying potential renewal risks
- Re-engaging previous clients and strengthening existing relationships
- Maintaining an accurate renewal pipeline and CRM records
- Working with internal teams to ensure a seamless client experience
- Achieving agreed retention, renewal and performance objectives

About You

You may have experience in account management, customer success, renewals, retention, consultative sales, business development, relationship management or contract management.

You'll bring:
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills
- A polished and professional approach to client relationships
- Confidence discussing pricing, contracts and value
- Strong relationship-building, influencing and negotiation skills
- Confidence handling objections and commercially sensitive conversations
- Excellent organisation and attention to detail
- The ability to manage multiple client relationships and renewal opportunities
- Confidence using CRM systems, with Microsoft Dynamics or similar experience advantageous

Experience within education, public sector, technology, software or another service-led organisation would also be beneficial.

Apply Now

If you have experience in client relationships, account management, renewals, retention, customer success or consultative sales and you're ready for a role where you can take genuine ownership of commercial relationships, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Business support officer
description:
Job Title: Business Support Officer

Temporary assignment: Up to 4 months. (Possibility to extend or convert to permanent)

Location: Newcastle

Salary: Based on 32,000 - 33,000 pa

Benefits:

Varied responsibilities across three departments, training available and exposure to engineering projects. Initial temporary assignment of approximately three to four months, with potential for a permanent opportunity, although this is not guaranteed.

The Company:

Theo James Recruitment is supporting a manufacturing and engineering business seeking a Business Process Support colleague to help its teams manage a busy workload.

Working alongside purchasing, engineering and programme management colleagues, you will contribute to day-to-day operations and help improve how information and documentation are organised.

Working Hours:

Monday - Friday - Office-based position.

Job Description:

As Business Process Support, you will coordinate administrative activities across Purchasing, Programme Management and Quality, keeping information accurate and following up on outstanding actions.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Raising sales orders, processing enquiries and issuing order acknowledgements.
- Supporting contract reviews by arranging discussions and maintaining checklists.
- Processing purchase orders and requisitions.
- Chasing suppliers and deliveries, escalating risks to schedules.
- Coordinating transport and maintaining shipment documentation.
- Updating ERP records and forecast information.
- Maintaining supplier certificates, approvals and quality documentation.
- Keeping QMS records and departmental folders organised.
- Liaising with accounts to resolve purchasing queries.
- Suggesting practical improvements to administrative processes.

The Business Process Support position involves quality administration rather than inspection. Technical, commercial and quality decisions remain with the relevant managers.

Skills & Experience:

For this Business Process Support opportunity, attitude, organisation and initiative are central to success.

We are looking for:
- Purchasing or supply-chain administration experience, ideally within manufacturing or engineering.
- Confidence chasing suppliers, influencing others and following actions through.
- Strong attention to detail and an understanding of the importance of accurate records.
- The ability to multitask and support several departments.
- A proactive approach and willingness to learn.

Epicor experience would be an advantage, although training can be provided. Experience in sales administration or document control would also be useful.

Why Should You Apply?

This Business Process Support role offers variety, involvement across multiple teams and the chance to make a visible difference to everyday operations.

You will bring organisation and initiative to a team that values a practical approach, while developing your knowledge of purchasing, programme support and quality administration.

Apply through Theo James Recruitment to discuss the Business Process Support opportunity.

title: Home Service Coordinator
description:
Home Service Coordinator

Newcastle-Under-Lyme (Hybrid working)

29,812.13 per annum pro rata

Hours per week: 37

Contract type: Fixed term until 31st March 2027

Delivering for people, dedicated to places

As our Home Service Coordinator, you'll play a vital role in ensuring our customers receive a seamless, customer-focused service across a range of housing maintenance and property-related workstreams, including repairs, voids, disrepair and compliance activity. You'll help keep customers at the heart of everything we do by ensuring services are well coordinated, efficiently managed and delivered right first time.

Working closely with customers, contractors, suppliers and internal teams, you'll coordinate activities from start to finish, ensuring appointments are scheduled effectively, work progresses smoothly and customers are kept informed every step of the way. Whether supporting a customer moving into their new home, helping to coordinate damp and mould and HHSRS interventions, arranging repairs and maintenance activity, you'll play an important role in delivering positive customer outcomes.

You'll also provide essential operational and administrative support across our maintenance services, ensuring accurate systems data, scheduling activity, timely and accurate asbestos surveys requests, processing supplier invoices and ensuring reporting and performance information are maintained. By working collaboratively across teams, responding proactively to customer enquiries and identifying opportunities for improvement, you'll help us deliver services that are simpler, slicker and smarter for both customers and colleagues.

What you'll need to succeed

We're looking for someone who is organised, customer-focused and enjoys building positive relationships with a wide range of people. You'll have experience coordinating services, managing competing priorities and delivering excellent customer service within a busy operational environment.

You'll be a confident communicator who can work effectively with customers, contractors and colleagues, ensuring information is accurate, timely and easy to understand. You'll be comfortable handling customer enquiries, resolving issues proactively and knowing when to escalate concerns to ensure the best possible outcome for our customers.

You'll have strong administrative and IT skills, with experience using housing systems to manage workloads, maintain accurate records and support performance reporting. Experience within housing, property services, maintenance, scheduling or contractor management would be advantageous, although your ability to coordinate services effectively and put customers first is what matters most.

Most importantly, you'll share our passion for delivering excellent customer experiences, embracing continuous improvement and working collaboratively to provide safe, decent homes and great services for our customers.

If you're ready to make a real difference to customers and communities, we'd love to hear from you.

In return we can offer you:
- Belonging to a team who make a difference to our community and value equality, diversity and inclusion.
- 22 days holiday + bank holidays + 3 concessionary days at Christmas
- Comprehensive employee assistance programme.
- Ongoing training and development in your role.
- A full benefits and discounts platform.
- Holiday buy, tech and annual savings schemes.
- Volunteer days.
- Competitive rates of pay.
- A generous company pension scheme.
- Wellbeing and stay safe provisions to look after you at work.

This role is subject to a basic DBS check.

NB Please note that we may interview whilst the role is live and may close this vacancy earlier than the advertised closing date if we receive a high volume of suitable applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible

title: Payroll & People Systems Assistant
description:
About us

National Energy Action (NEA) is the national fuel poverty charity. We have worked across England, Wales, and Northern Ireland for over 40 years to ensure that everyone can afford to live in a warm, healthy home.

Millions of households across the UK still face high energy bills, low incomes and poor energy efficiency. We work with frontline practitioners, companies, regulators and governments to support vulnerable clients, raise awareness and achieve enduring change. Our work tackles these challenges head on, delivering practical support, influencing policy and improving lives.

Our values guide how we work every day - we make things happen, we put people first and we lead the way. These values come to life through our behaviours, including pulling together, owning the outcome and supporting one another.

Our teams are friendly, knowledgeable and passionate about what we do. We offer a supportive, rewarding workplace where you can build a meaningful career while making a real difference every day.

The Role

We are looking for a motivated and committed Payroll & HR Systems Assistant to join our Support Services Directorate. This shared service role supports both the Finance and People & Culture teams, ensuring payroll is processed accurately and on time, employee records are maintained correctly, and HR systems operate effectively.

This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to a respected national charity while developing your payroll and HR systems experience in a collaborative and supportive environment.

What you'll be doing
- Prepare and process monthly salary calculations and maintain payroll records
- Support statutory payroll requirements including PAYE, National Insurance, pensions and RTI
- Prepare, reconcile and post monthly payroll journals and process payroll related payments
- Respond to payroll queries and support year end processes including P60s and P11 Ds
- Maintain accurate employee records within Iris Cascade and support employee lifecycle administration
- Produce regular and ad hoc people reports and support data quality checks
- Work with Finance and People teams to ensure payroll and HR data remain aligned
- Support HR systems testing, reporting developments and continuous improvement
- Assist with the effective administration of HR systems and processes

Your work will directly support NEA's ability to maintain accurate payroll and people information, meet statutory requirements and provide effective support to colleagues across the organisation.

What you will need to succeed

You will bring:
- Experience preparing payroll calculations and processing payroll through a payroll system
- Experience maintaining employee data within an HR, people management or payroll system
- Experience producing reports and maintaining confidential payroll records
- Strong understanding of UK payroll legislation including PAYE, NI, pensions and statutory payments
- Knowledge of pension auto enrolment requirements
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to work to strict deadlines
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- Effective communication skills and the ability to handle sensitive information confidentially
- GCSE (or equivalent) in English and Maths (Grade C/4 or above)

Desirable:
- Experience using Iris Cascade, Sage 50 Payroll or similar systems
- Experience preparing payroll journals and financial reconciliations
- Experience supporting payroll audits and year end processes
- Experience working within a Finance, Payroll or shared service environment
- Understanding of HR processes including onboarding and contractual changes
- Payroll qualification (e.g. CIPP) or equivalent training

What we offer
- £16,364-£17,164 per annum (pro-rata) Level 2, Points 6-9. New appointments will usually begin at the starting point of the scale.
- 11.5% non contributory pension.
- 25 days annual leave plus 3 additional days between Christmas and New Year when our offices are closed. Entitlement is pro-rata for part-time staff
- All public holidays.
- Flexible working arrangements including hybrid working.
- Enhanced family friendly payments.
- Employee Assistance Programme.
- Employee benefits platform.

This is a hybrid role based at NEA's Newcastle office, with a minimum of one day per week on site.

Hybrid and home working are subject to necessary H&S and GDPR compliance checks. Post holders must be resident within the UK and be able to provide their Right to Work in the UK.

Please note that National Energy Action is not a sponsoring organisation. Therefore, the successful applicant must already possess the right to work in the UK or be able to secure the right to work in the UK independently.

Please note CVs will not be accepted as part of the application process. No recruitment agency or advertising enquiries, please.

NEA is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all people with the necessary skills and experience.

Only shortlisted candidates selected for interview will be notified of the confirmed time and location of interview.

title: Sales Executive
description:
We have an exciting opportunity for an experienced Internal Sales Executive to join a growing, successful business providing technical services and solutions to the UK construction industry.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys B2 B sales, outbound calling, and developing customer relationships. You ll be responsible for generating new business opportunities while also managing and growing an established portfolio of customers.

The Role

As an Internal Sales Executive, you will:
- Make proactive outbound calls to prospective B2 B customers
- Identify key decision-makers and generate new business opportunities
- Qualify prospects to understand their requirements, budgets and upcoming projects
- Book qualified appointments and opportunities for field-based Business Development Managers
- Manage and develop an existing portfolio of smaller B2 B accounts
- Re-engage dormant customers and identify opportunities to increase spend
- Identify cross-selling and up-selling opportunities
- Respond to sales enquiries, quotes and orders generated through your activity
- Maintain accurate customer and sales information within the CRM
- Build strong, long-term relationships with customers across the UK

About You

To be considered for this role, you should have:
- Previous experience within B2 B telesales, internal sales, lead generation or business development
- Proven experience making outbound calls and working towards sales targets
- Confidence overcoming objections and speaking with key decision-makers
- A strong telephone manner with excellent rapport-building and questioning skills
- The ability to identify and qualify genuine commercial opportunities
- Good organisational and time-management skills
- Experience using CRM systems and Microsoft Office
- A proactive, resilient and self-motivated approach to sales

Experience within construction supplies, plant hire, tool hire, technical services, engineering or industrial sectors would be advantageous, although this is not essential.

Previous experience as a Sales Development Representative (SDR), Appointment Setter, Telesales Executive, Internal Sales Executive or Business Development Executive would also be highly relevant.

What s on Offer
- Opportunity to work from Leeds or the Northeast
- Established portfolio of existing B2 B customers
- Genuine opportunity to generate and develop new business
- Work with an established and growing national organisation
- Support from experienced field-based Business Development Managers
- Varied role combining new business development and account management
- Excellent opportunity for long-term career development

Additional Information

This is a proactive sales position and will suit someone who genuinely enjoys picking up the phone, building relationships and creating commercial opportunities. The role has a target of approximately 35 proactive outbound calls per day, split between new business development and existing account management.

Due to the high volume of applications, we aim to respond to all candidates, although this is not always possible. If you have not been contacted within 5 days, please assume your application has not been successful on this occasion. However, we may retain your details for future opportunities.

description: We are looking to recruit an enthusiastic individual to join our well established reception team for 30 - 37 hours per week, working Monday to Friday between the hours of 7:45 and 18:30 You are the first voice patients hear and the first face they see when they visit the surgery. We pride ourselves on our consistent professional, compassionate and caring attitude towards all patients and visitors to the practice. Work collaboratively with clinicians and administrative colleagues to support practice operations. Assist with the smooth day-to-day running of reception and administrative functions.
